text:
maria_support: Customer reported intermittent 503s during streaming calls from their EU region. They included a request_id and a short log excerpt. asking for help to get a reproducible curl so we can debug.

maria_support: request_id: rq_8b3c1f2a; time range: 2026-03-15T14:02:10-14:07:00Z. Customer says it happens ~2-3x per hour during long streaming responses (10s+). Logs snippet they pasted: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and `connection reset by peer`.

dev_jordan: thanks — can you ask them to run a minimal curl that preserves headers + raw output so we can see chunk boundaries? suggest this exact command and ask them to capture stdout/stderr: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -X POST \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs?model=gpt-neo-stream&stream=true \n  -d '{"input":"stream test
repeat lines to force long output"}' --http1.1 > curl_stdout.txt 2> curl_stderr.txt
```

dev_jordan: ask them to attach both files and grep for `request-id` header in curl_stderr.txt (curl prints response headers there with -v). If they get a 503, we need the server response headers (x-request-id, x-region, x-node).

maria_support: relayed command to customer and asked them to run it and upload both files. also asked them to include their client IP and whether they're behind a proxy.

infra-bot: logs: linked internal logs for rq_8b3c1f2a -> https://internal.redwood/logs/requests/rq_8b3c1f2a (access: dev_jordan, ops_rita).

ops_rita: pulled the internal logs, I can see a pattern of connection resets on node eu-3 around 14:03:xx. forwarding kernel logs and nginx error lines. snippet: `2026-03-15T14:03:12Z eu-3 nginx[2345]: *12456 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 18.205.33.12, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/outputs?model=gpt-neo-stream&stream=true HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.2.0.45:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai"`

dev_jordan: thanks — two quick asks: 1) if customer curl shows `x-request-id` from our servers (should be in stderr) please paste that exact header; 2) we need their debug bundle (we provide a small script) to capture tcpdump + client TLS handshake timing. sending bundle command: 
```
# run as root on customer machine; produces debug-bundle.tgz
sudo tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/stream-debug.pcap tcp and host api.redwood.ai &
# in another shell run the curl above until you hit the failure, then stop tcpdump
sudo killall tcpdump
tar czf debug-bundle.tgz /tmp/stream-debug.pcap curl_stdout.txt curl_stderr.txt
```

maria_support: customer replied with curl_stdout.txt (attached) and curl_stderr.txt. They reported `x-request-id: rq_8b3c1f2a` in the server headers, and the stderr shows a `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable`. Their stdout contains partial SSE chunks, then EOF.

dev_jordan: excellent. could you paste the first 5 lines of curl_stderr.txt here (redact API key)? also ask customer to run the curl with `--raw` so curl doesn't attempt to process CRLFs: 
```
curl --raw -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs?model=gpt-neo-stream&stream=true \
  -d '{"input":"stream test long output"}' --http1.1 > raw_out.txt 2> raw_err.txt
```

maria_support: pasted lines from their stderr (redacted):
```
*   Trying 3.125.45.10:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (3.125.45.10) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/outputs?model=gpt-neo-stream&stream=true HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/8.2.1
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< content-type: text/event-stream
< x-request-id: rq_8b3c1f2a
< x-node: eu-3
< x-region: eu-west-1
```

ops_rita: kernel logs show `reset peer` at the same timestamp; doesn't look like our process OOMs. Could be an upstream worker crash or a transient network blip on eu-3. I'll pull the process logs from the model workers and attach them.

dev_jordan: next steps: 1) request debug-bundle.tgz from the customer; 2) I'll run a repro from our own lab directed at eu-3 using a synthetic long input to try to trigger the same behavior; 3) if reproduced, we'll capture pprof and memory snapshots. In parallel, ops_rita can correlate node restarts.

maria_support: customer said they'll run tcpdump and produce debug-bundle.tgz, ETA ~30m. asked them to upload to the secure upload link: https://uploads.redwood.ai/sup/ and paste the resulting URL in this thread.

infra-bot: note: created incident-bridge ticket IB-2026-334 for tracking (linked to rq_8b3c1f2a).

dev_jordan: thanks everyone. once we have the bundle I'll triage and paste exact repro steps (curl + flags) to validate a fix. :thumbsup:
